text:
amelia: Hey team — customer Sam from AcmeGames reporting a sudden `401 invalid_api_key` on all hosted inference calls after their last CI deploy. They say nothing changed in code, just deployed an image.

sam: Repro steps I got from them: 
1) CI sets env API_KEY from secret store
2) app reads process.env.REDFWOOD_API_KEY (they named it REDFWOOD_API_KEY in their pipeline)
3) curl to our endpoint returns 401 with x-request-id header set.

sam: Their example curl (sanitized):
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer rk_prod_AbCdEf123456-9f2c1d7" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate
```

amelia: I asked them for the raw header from their logs — they pasted this (weird):
```
Authorization: Bearer rk_prod_AbCdEf123456-9f2c1d7-9d1c4f0
```

nina: aha, looks like the key has an extra suffix `-9d1c4f0` appended. Could be CI expanding a var like `$GIT_COMMIT` when interpolating secrets or a template mistake.

leo: @nina can you check if our hosted auth layer trims or validates token format? If a dash-suffix is allowed it may map to a different key id; but most of our keys are strict pattern matching.

nina: Quick check — auth service expects regex `^rk_(prod|stg)_[A-Za-z0-9]{12,}` and rejects anything after a non-alphanumeric suffix. So extra `-9d1c4f0` will cause invalid_api_key.

amelia: I asked the customer for their CI job YAML. They pasted a snippet where they build a composite env var: 
```
env:
  REDWOOD_API_KEY: "${{ secrets.REDWOOD_API_KEY }}-${{ github.sha }}"
```

sam: They say ops engineer added that to stamp images with commit id — unintentionally appended the git sha to the secret at runtime.

amelia: Recommended immediate mitigation to customer: revert to the original secret (remove suffix) or create a new key and deploy without the suffix. Also warned them not to paste the suffixed key into dashboard since rotated keys would likely keep failing.

sam: I asked them to try removing the suffix locally; they tested `curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer rk_prod_AbCdEf123456" ...` and it returned 200. They confirmed flows work again.

leo: Marking as user error/CI templating mistake. We should add guidance to our support KB: common CI templating gotchas (GH Actions `${{ github.sha }}`, GitLab `$CI_COMMIT_SHA`, and shell concatenation).

nina: Also adding quick server-side improvement ticket: auth logs should include a hint on format mismatch (e.g., "received token contains invalid suffix" rather than generic invalid_api_key) — filing ENG-7882 for stronger debug message.

ops-bot: Incident note created: support/6211112222 - customer CI appended commit hash to API key; resolved by removing suffix (owner: amelia).

amelia: Closing thread with customer: they regenerated a new key, removed the auto-stamp from CI, and confirmed no further 401s. Asked them to rotate keys if they think the old (suffixed) value was stored anywhere. :white_check_mark:

sam: Thanks everyone! :pray:

nina: Follow-up: adding CI templating paragraph to onboarding docs and a small FAQ blurb. :memo:
